But ṣaydalī (which still can take the pl. ṣanādilaẗ !) is originally a *‘seller of sandal powder’ (used in medicine) – Rolland2014a. (A variant of † ṣandalī , † ṣandalānī , is attested, for instance, in Wahrmund1887 or, for OttTu, in Redhouse1890 with the meaning ‘dealer in sandal wood, druggist and perfumer’.) Thus, ṣaydalī is based on ↗ ṣandal ‘sandal wood’ (which is of ultimately Ind origin). ▪ [v2] … – ▪ [v1] ↗ ṣandal . ▪ [v2] … ▪ [v1] ↗ ṣandal . ▪ [v2] … – – Sources ; meta ; gram ; engl ; conc ; hist ; cogn ; disc ; west ; deriv ;
